what: detached, checkpointed Tamper solve at the adaptive chamber
authority: Matt 2026-08-05 (grow the chamber); coordinator: launch if standing gates go green

conventions.objective: asymmetric at the pre-registered phi_floor and w
conventions.read: envelope (argmin over the arm's own trajectory)
conventions.baseline: uniform doping, scored at its OWN matched read

deviations_from_phase_e: lc_part 2.5e-3 vs 0.9375e-3: the Tamper's own tessellation carries a 0.105 mm minimum edge, so any conforming mesh inherits ~0.092 mm elements and the explicit CFL substep follows independently of lc_part. Refining adds cells without buying back a time step.
max_time_s 900 vs 650: at 150 s this part is at 110.8 C mean heading to a ~365 C plateau; 650 s would stop it before melt and hand the envelope a degenerate argmin.

harvest.resume: re-run the same command; arms already in phase_e_tamper.json are skipped and the solve arm warm-restarts from the checkpoint's best iterate with the remaining budget
harvest.resume_caveat: a resume is a WARM RESTART, not bit-identical: scipy does not expose L-BFGS-B's curvature memory, so it is rebuilt (solve3d/phase_e/checkpoint.py)

expected_cost.note: a 150 s march on this mesh took 469 s wall, so a 900 s forward is roughly 47 min and a 40 forward-equivalent budget is of order 30 hours. The checkpoint is what makes that survivable; per-evaluation writes are atomic.
expected_cost.binding_cost: the STL's 0.105 mm minimum tessellation edge, not the chamber and not lc_part

not_yet_delivered: the solved-vs-uniform verdict and the deck figures; both need this run to finish

chamber_tag_discrepancy.why: the feasibility check ran with precomp_coeffs=None; the live run has Level 0 pre-compensation ON by default, which grows the part span from 44.40 mm to 45.77 mm (xy_scale 1.030928), so the adaptive rule returns 86 mm rather than 85 mm
chamber_tag_discrepancy.note: a 1 mm difference is physically immaterial here -- the EQS sweep shows in-part Q non-uniformity moving only -0.19 percent between 85 and 100 mm -- but it is recorded rather than blurred, and the TAG is what surfaced it. That is the tagging convention doing its job on its first live run.

budget_discrepancy.recommendation: harvest at 12 gradient evaluations for the pre-registered 40 forward-equivalent comparison; any evaluations beyond that are a LABELLED extension, not the pre-registered budget. The per-evaluation checkpoint makes either stopping point available without re-running.

budget_ruling.reason: 12 gradient evaluations IS the pre-registered 40 forward-equivalents at Phase C's measured 3.328 fwd-eq per evaluation. Pre-registration wins over the CLI flag's accidental semantics.
budget_ruling.beyond_12: runs only if Matt explicitly extends; would be a labelled extension
budget_ruling.implementation: relaunched with --budget 12 rather than watching for eval 12, so the run SELF-TERMINATES and scores itself. Resumed from the eval-1 checkpoint; nothing lost, since best_v was still the uniform start (all 1.0).
